+"""Scraper for metacritic.com game pages.
+
+Metacritic serves Nuxt-rendered HTML: every page carries the data its components were
+rendered from in a `__NUXT_DATA__` devalue payload. We decode that payload rather than
+scraping the DOM, because the markup is generated Tailwind soup while the payload is
+the site's own typed model.
+
+Reviews additionally have a JSON backend (the same one the page calls for pagination);
+we use it when it answers and fall back to the SSR page otherwise.
+
+Parsing is kept separate from fetching (`parse_*` vs `fetch_*`) so the tests can run
+against saved fixtures without touching the network.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import logging
+import re
+from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from selectolax.parser import HTMLParser
+
+from app.config import settings
+from app.scraper.devalue import extract_nuxt_payload
+from app.scraper.http import PoliteClient, ScrapeError, default_client
+
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+ReviewKind = Literal["critic", "user"]
+
+NEW_RELEASES_COUNT = 20
+
+_JSON_LD_RE = re.compile(r'<script type="application/ld\+json">(.*?)</script>', re.DOTALL)
+_SLUG_RE = re.compile(r"^/game/([a-z0-9\-]+)/?$")
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- models
+
+
+@dataclass
+class PlatformScore:
+    """One platform release of a game. Either score may be missing."""
+
+    name: str
+    slug: str | None = None
+    metascore: int | None = None
+    userscore: float | None = None
+
+
+@dataclass
+class GameData:
+    title: str
+    slug: str
+    metacritic_url: str
+    cover_url: str | None = None
+    description: str | None = None
+    developer: str | None = None
+    publisher: str | None = None
+    release_date: str | None = None
+    genres: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    platforms: list[PlatformScore] = field(default_factory=list)
+    video_url: str | None = None
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return asdict(self)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Review:
+    text: str
+    score: float | None
+    author: str | None
+    date: str | None
+    kind: ReviewKind = "critic"
+    platform: str | None = None
+    url: str | None = None
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return asdict(self)
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------- payload helpers
+
+
+def _page_components(html: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Components of the page's own `loadPage:...` entry (skipping the site skeleton)."""
+    payload = extract_nuxt_payload(html)
+    data = payload.get("data") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
+    if not isinstance(data, dict):
+        raise ScrapeError("nuxt payload has no `data` section")
+    for key, node in data.items():
+        if not key.startswith("loadPage:") or key.startswith("loadPage:skeleton"):
+            continue
+        if isinstance(node, dict) and isinstance(node.get("components"), list):
+            return node["components"]
+    raise ScrapeError("no page components found in nuxt payload")
+
+
+def _component(components: list[dict[str, Any]], name: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+    for component in components:
+        meta = component.get("meta") or {}
+        if meta.get("componentName") == name:
+            return component.get("data") or {}
+    return None
+
+
+def _json_ld(html: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """First JSON-LD block on the page, or `{}`."""
+    for match in _JSON_LD_RE.finditer(html):
+        try:
+            data = json.loads(match.group(1))
+        except json.JSONDecodeError:
+            continue
+        if isinstance(data, dict):
+            return data
+    return {}
+
+
+def _slugs_from_links(nodes) -> list[str]:
+    """Slugs of `/game/<slug>/` links, de-duplicated, in document order."""
+    slugs: list[str] = []
+    for node in nodes:
+        match = _SLUG_RE.match(node.attributes.get("href", "") or "")
+        if match and match.group(1) not in slugs:
+            slugs.append(match.group(1))
+    return slugs
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------------- listings
+
+
+def parse_new_releases(html: str, limit: int = NEW_RELEASES_COUNT) -> list[str]:
+    """Slugs of the "New Releases" carousel on https://www.metacritic.com/game/."""
+    try:
+        data = _component(_page_components(html), "new-releases-carousel")
+    except ScrapeError:
+        data = None
+    if data and isinstance(data.get("items"), list):
+        slugs = [item["slug"] for item in data["items"] if item.get("slug")]
+        if slugs:
+            return slugs[:limit]
+
+    log.warning("new-releases-carousel missing from payload, falling back to markup")
+    carousel = HTMLParser(html).css_first('[data-testid="new-game-release-carousel"]')
+    if carousel is None:
+        raise ScrapeError("New Releases section not found on the games front door")
+    return _slugs_from_links(carousel.css('a[href^="/game/"]'))[:limit]
+
+
+def parse_browse_page(html: str) -> list[str]:
+    """Slugs of the result cards on a /browse/game/... page."""
+    tree = HTMLParser(html)
+    slugs: list[str] = []
+    for card in tree.css('[data-testid="filter-results"]'):
+        slugs.extend(s for s in _slugs_from_links(card.css('a[href^="/game/"]')) if s not in slugs)
+    if not slugs:
+        raise ScrapeError("no result cards found on browse page")
+    return slugs
+
+
+def fetch_new_releases(
+    limit: int = NEW_RELEASES_COUNT, client: PoliteClient | None = None
+) -> list[str]:
+    """First `limit` slugs from the New Releases section of the Games front door."""
+    client = client or default_client()
+    html = client.get_text(f"{settings.metacritic_base_url}/game/")
+    return parse_new_releases(html, limit=limit)
+
+
+def fetch_browse_new(page: int = 1, client: PoliteClient | None = None) -> list[str]:
+    """Slugs from page `page` of "SEE ALL / New" (24 games per page)."""
+    if page < 1:
+        raise ValueError("page is 1-based")
+    client = client or default_client()
+    url = f"{settings.metacritic_base_url}/browse/game/all/all/all-time/new/"
+    html = client.get_text(url, params={"page": page})
+    return parse_browse_page(html)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- game details
+
+
+def _cover_url(images: list[dict[str, Any]], json_ld: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
+    """Best cover image: the portrait card art if the page has one, else the hero shot.
+
+    The `<img>` tags on the page point at signed `/a/img/resize/<hash>/…` derivatives.
+    Those signatures do not survive being replayed — Metacritic answers 403 "Invalid
+    hash" for them outside the original page render — so we address the untouched
+    original in the asset bucket instead, which is served unsigned.
+    """
+    by_type = {img.get("typeName"): img for img in images if isinstance(img, dict)}
+    image = by_type.get("cardImage") or by_type.get("mainImage") or (images[0] if images else None)
+    if isinstance(image, dict):
+        bucket_type, bucket_path = image.get("bucketType"), image.get("bucketPath")
+        if bucket_type and bucket_path:
+            return f"{settings.metacritic_base_url}/a/img/{bucket_type}{bucket_path}"
+    return json_ld.get("image") or None
+
+
+def _company(companies: list[dict[str, Any]], type_name: str) -> str | None:
+    for company in companies:
+        if isinstance(company, dict) and company.get("typeName") == type_name:
+            return company.get("name")
+    return None
+
+
+def _video_url(item: dict[str, Any], json_ld: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
+    video = item.get("video")
+    if isinstance(video, dict):
+        for key in ("embedUrl", "url", "manifestUrl"):
+            if video.get(key):
+                return video[key]
+    trailer = json_ld.get("trailer")
+    if isinstance(trailer, dict):
+        for key in ("embedUrl", "contentUrl", "url"):
+            if trailer.get(key):
+                return trailer[key]
+    return None
+
+
+def _score(summary: Any) -> Any:
+    """Score out of a score summary, or `None` when Metacritic would render "tbd".
+
+    Below its minimum review count the site reports `score: 0` with a null `sentiment`
+    instead of omitting the score, which would otherwise look like a real zero.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(summary, dict):
+        return None
+    if summary.get("score") is None or not summary.get("sentiment"):
+        return None
+    return summary["score"]
+
+
+def parse_game(html: str, slug: str) -> GameData:
+    """Build :class:`GameData` from a saved `/game/<slug>/` page.
+
+    Per-platform *user* scores are not on this page — see
+    :func:`fetch_platform_user_score`; here they stay `None` except for the platform
+    the page itself is about.
+    """
+    components = _page_components(html)
+    data = _component(components, "product")
+    if not data or not isinstance(data.get("item"), dict):
+        raise ScrapeError(f"no product component on the page for {slug!r}")
+    item = data["item"]
+    json_ld = _json_ld(html)
+
+    production = item.get("production") or {}
+    companies = production.get("companies") or []
+
+    platforms = [
+        PlatformScore(
+            name=platform.get("name") or "",
+            slug=platform.get("slug"),
+            metascore=_score(platform.get("criticScoreSummary")),
+        )
+        for platform in item.get("platforms") or []
+        if isinstance(platform, dict) and platform.get("name")
+    ]
+
+    # The page is rendered for one lead platform; its user score is in the payload.
+    lead_summary = _component(components, "user-score-summary") or {}
+    lead_user_score = _score(lead_summary.get("item"))
+    lead_name = item.get("platform")
+    for platform in platforms:
+        if platform.name == lead_name:
+            platform.userscore = lead_user_score
+
+    return GameData(
+        title=item.get("title") or "",
+        slug=item.get("slug") or slug,
+        metacritic_url=f"{settings.metacritic_base_url}/game/{item.get('slug') or slug}/",
+        cover_url=_cover_url(item.get("images") or [], json_ld),
+        description=item.get("description") or json_ld.get("description") or None,
+        developer=_company(companies, "Developer"),
+        publisher=_company(companies, "Publisher"),
+        release_date=item.get("releaseDate") or item.get("releaseDateText"),
+        genres=[
+            g["name"] for g in item.get("genres") or [] if isinstance(g, dict) and g.get("name")
+        ],
+        platforms=platforms,
+        video_url=_video_url(item, json_ld),
+    )
+
+
+def parse_platform_user_score(source: str | dict[str, Any]) -> float | None:
+    """User score out of a `/user-reviews/?platform=...` page or its API response."""
+    if isinstance(source, str):
+        components = _page_components(source)
+    else:
+        components = source.get("components") or []
+    return _score((_component(components, "user-score-summary") or {}).get("item"))
+
+
+def fetch_platform_user_score(
+    slug: str, platform_slug: str, client: PoliteClient | None = None
+) -> float | None:
+    """User score for one platform release, via the JSON backend or the SSR page."""
+    client = client or default_client()
+    api_url = (
+        f"{settings.metacritic_api_url}/composer/metacritic/pages/"
+        f"games-user-reviews/{slug}/platform/{platform_slug}/web"
+    )
+    try:
+        return parse_platform_user_score(
+            client.get_json(api_url, params={"apiKey": settings.metacritic_api_key})
+        )
+    except (ScrapeError, ValueError) as exc:
+        log.warning("user-score API failed for %s/%s: %s", slug, platform_slug, exc)
+
+    html = client.get_text(
+        f"{settings.metacritic_base_url}/game/{slug}/user-reviews/",
+        params={"platform": platform_slug},
+    )
+    return parse_platform_user_score(html)
+
+
+def fetch_game(
+    slug: str,
+    client: PoliteClient | None = None,
+    *,
+    platform_user_scores: bool = True,
+) -> GameData:
+    """Full card for one game.
+
+    With `platform_user_scores` (the default) each platform costs one extra request,
+    because Metacritic only renders the user score of the platform being viewed.
+    """
+    client = client or default_client()
+    html = client.get_text(f"{settings.metacritic_base_url}/game/{slug}/")
+    game = parse_game(html, slug)
+
+    if platform_user_scores:
+        for platform in game.platforms:
+            if platform.userscore is not None or not platform.slug:
+                continue
+            try:
+                platform.userscore = fetch_platform_user_score(slug, platform.slug, client)
+            except (ScrapeError, ValueError) as exc:
+                log.warning("no user score for %s on %s: %s", slug, platform.slug, exc)
+    return game
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- reviews
+
+
+def _review_from_item(item: dict[str, Any], kind: ReviewKind) -> Review | None:
+    text = (item.get("quote") or "").strip()
+    if not text:
+        return None
+    if kind == "critic":
+        author = item.get("publicationName") or item.get("author") or None
+    else:
+        author = item.get("author") or None
+    return Review(
+        text=text,
+        score=item.get("score"),
+        author=author,
+        date=item.get("date"),
+        kind=kind,
+        platform=item.get("platform"),
+        url=item.get("url"),
+    )
+
+
+def _reviews_from_items(items: Any, kind: ReviewKind, limit: int) -> list[Review]:
+    if not isinstance(items, list):
+        return []
+    reviews = (_review_from_item(i, kind) for i in items if isinstance(i, dict))
+    return [r for r in reviews if r is not None][:limit]
+
+
+def parse_reviews_page(html: str, kind: ReviewKind, limit: int = 40) -> list[Review]:
+    """Reviews from a saved `/critic-reviews/` or `/user-reviews/` page."""
+    data = _component(_page_components(html), f"{kind}-reviews")
+    if data is None:
+        raise ScrapeError(f"no {kind}-reviews component on the page")
+    return _reviews_from_items(data.get("items"), kind, limit)
+
+
+def parse_reviews_api(payload: dict[str, Any], kind: ReviewKind, limit: int = 40) -> list[Review]:
+    """Reviews from a backend.metacritic.com reviews response."""
+    return _reviews_from_items((payload.get("data") or {}).get("items"), kind, limit)
+
+
+def fetch_reviews(
+    slug: str,
+    kind: ReviewKind = "critic",
+    limit: int = 40,
+    client: PoliteClient | None = None,
+) -> list[Review]:
+    """Up to `limit` reviews of one kind.
+
+    Prefers the JSON backend (the SSR page only ships the first batch) and falls back
+    to the page itself.
+    """
+    if kind not in ("critic", "user"):
+        raise ValueError(f"kind must be 'critic' or 'user', got {kind!r}")
+    client = client or default_client()
+
+    api_url = f"{settings.metacritic_api_url}/reviews/metacritic/{kind}/games/{slug}/web"
+    reviews: list[Review] = []
+    try:
+        # The backend caps a page well below `limit` (10 for critics, 50 for users),
+        # so keep asking for the next offset until we have enough or it runs dry.
+        offset = 0
+        while len(reviews) < limit:
+            payload = client.get_json(
+                api_url,
+                params={
+                    "apiKey": settings.metacritic_api_key,
+                    "offset": offset,
+                    "limit": limit - len(reviews),
+                    "filterBySentiment": "all",
+                    "sort": "score" if kind == "critic" else "date",
+                },
+            )
+            items = (payload.get("data") or {}).get("items") or []
+            if not items:
+                break
+            reviews.extend(parse_reviews_api(payload, kind, limit - len(reviews)))
+            offset += len(items)
+            if offset >= (payload.get("data") or {}).get("totalResults", 0):
+                break
+        if reviews:
+            return reviews
+        log.warning("reviews API returned nothing for %s/%s, falling back to HTML", slug, kind)
+    except (ScrapeError, ValueError) as exc:
+        log.warning("reviews API failed for %s/%s: %s", slug, kind, exc)
+
+    html = client.get_text(f"{settings.metacritic_base_url}/game/{slug}/{kind}-reviews/")
+    return parse_reviews_page(html, kind, limit)
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ cli
+
+
+def _main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
+    """`python -m app.scraper.metacritic [slug ...]` — live check against the site."""
+    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
+    client = default_client()
+
+    slugs = argv[1:]
+    if not slugs:
+        slugs = fetch_new_releases(client=client)[:3]
+        print(f"# New Releases (first 3 of {NEW_RELEASES_COUNT}): {', '.join(slugs)}\n")
+
+    for slug in slugs:
+        game = fetch_game(slug, client=client)
+        out = game.to_dict()
+        out["critic_reviews"] = [r.to_dict() for r in fetch_reviews(slug, "critic", 3, client)]
+        out["user_reviews"] = [r.to_dict() for r in fetch_reviews(slug, "user", 3, client)]
+        print(json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
+    return 0
+

+    import sys
+
+    raise SystemExit(_main(sys.argv))

+"""Similar games by TF-IDF cosine over the game's own text. No LLM, no extra deps.
+
+A few hundred games make a matrix small enough to keep in memory and rebuild whenever
+the row count changes.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+import re
+from collections import Counter
+
+from sqlalchemy import func, select
+
+from app.db import SessionLocal
+from app.models import Game
+
+_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[a-zа-яё0-9]{3,}", re.IGNORECASE)
+
+# Words that appear in half the marketing blurbs and carry no signal.
+_STOPWORDS = frozenset(
+    """the and for with you your this that from are was has have not but all can its
+    new game games play player players world can will one out more into their они
+    очень игра игры""".split()
+)
+
+_cache: tuple[int, list[int], list[dict[str, float]]] | None = None
+
+
+def _document(game: Game) -> str:
+    parts = [
+        game.title or "",
+        game.title or "",  # the title matters more than the blurb — count it twice
+        " ".join(game.genres or []),
+        " ".join(game.genres or []),
+        game.developer or "",
+        game.publisher or "",
+        " ".join(p.name for p in game.platforms),
+        game.description or "",
+    ]
+    return " ".join(parts).lower()
+
+
+def _tokenize(text: str) -> list[str]:
+    return [w for w in _WORD_RE.findall(text) if w not in _STOPWORDS]
+
+
+def _build() -> tuple[int, list[int], list[dict[str, float]]]:
+    with SessionLocal() as session:
+        games = session.scalars(select(Game).order_by(Game.id)).all()
+        docs = [Counter(_tokenize(_document(g))) for g in games]
+        ids = [g.id for g in games]
+
+    n = len(docs)
+    df = Counter(term for doc in docs for term in doc)
+    vectors: list[dict[str, float]] = []
+    for doc in docs:
+        total = sum(doc.values()) or 1
+        vector = {
+            term: (count / total) * math.log((n + 1) / (df[term] + 1))
+            for term, count in doc.items()
+        }
+        norm = math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in vector.values())) or 1.0
+        vectors.append({t: v / norm for t, v in vector.items()})
+    return n, ids, vectors
+
+
+def _vectors() -> tuple[list[int], list[dict[str, float]]]:
+    global _cache
+    with SessionLocal() as session:
+        count = session.scalar(select(func.count(Game.id))) or 0
+    if _cache is None or _cache[0] != count:
+        _cache = _build()
+    return _cache[1], _cache[2]
+
+
+def invalidate() -> None:
+    """Force a rebuild — call after a crawl edits existing rows."""
+    global _cache
+    _cache = None
+
+
+def similar_games(game_id: int, k: int = 6) -> list[tuple[int, float]]:
+    """Up to `k` (game_id, score) pairs, most similar first."""
+    ids, vectors = _vectors()
+    if game_id not in ids:
+        return []
+    target = vectors[ids.index(game_id)]
+
+    scored = []
+    for other_id, vector in zip(ids, vectors, strict=True):
+        if other_id == game_id:
+            continue
+        # Iterate the shorter vector; both are unit length, so the dot product is cosine.
+        small, large = (target, vector) if len(target) < len(vector) else (vector, target)
+        score = sum(weight * large.get(term, 0.0) for term, weight in small.items())
+        if score > 0:
+            scored.append((other_id, score))
+    scored.sort(key=lambda pair: (-pair[1], pair[0]))
+    return scored[:k]

@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@
+{# Metacritic's own thresholds: green >= 75, yellow 50-74, red < 50. #}
+{% macro score_class(value, max) %}
+  {%- if value is none -%}tbd
+  {%- elif value >= 0.75 * max -%}good
+  {%- elif value >= 0.50 * max -%}mixed
+  {%- else -%}bad
+  {%- endif -%}
+{% endmacro %}
+
+{% macro score_badge(value, max, label) %}
+  <span class="score score--{{ score_class(value, max) | trim }}"
+        title="{{ label }}: {{ value if value is not none else 'нет оценки' }}">
+    {{ value if value is not none else 'tbd' }}
+  </span>
+{% endmacro %}
+
+{# Prefer our own cached copy; metacritic.com answers 403 for hotlinked covers. #}
+{% macro cover(game, sizes) %}
+  {% set src = "/covers/" ~ game.cover_path if game.cover_path else game.cover_url %}
+  {% if src %}
+    <img class="cover__img" src="{{ src }}" alt="Обложка: {{ game.title }}"
+         loading="lazy" sizes="{{ sizes }}">
+  {% else %}
+    <span class="cover__empty" aria-hidden="true">{{ game.title[:1] }}</span>
+  {% endif %}
+{% endmacro %}

+<script>
+(() => {
+  const $ = (s) => document.querySelector(s);
+  const conn = $("#conn"), log = $("#log"), runBtn = $("#run"), runMsg = $("#run-msg");
+  const MAX_ROWS = 200;
+
+  const setConn = (cls, text) => { conn.className = "conn conn--" + cls; conn.textContent = text; };
+
+  function renderState(s) {
+    for (const [name, w] of Object.entries(s.workers)) {
+      const li = document.querySelector(`[data-worker="${name}"]`);
+      if (!li) continue;
+      li.querySelector(".worker__dot").className = "worker__dot worker__dot--" + w.status;
+      li.querySelector(".worker__state").textContent = w.status + (w.detail ? " · " + w.detail : "");
+    }
+    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(s.today)) {
+      const el = document.querySelector(`#today [data-k="${k}"]`);
+      if (el) el.textContent = k === "llm_cost" ? Number(v).toFixed(4) : v;
+    }
+    const box = $("#run-box"), r = s.run;
+    if (r) {
+      const done = r.processed + r.failed;
+      box.innerHTML = `<p class="mon__line">#${r.id} · ${r.source} · ${r.reason} · начат ${r.started_at}</p>
+        <progress class="bar" value="${done}" max="${r.planned || 1}"></progress>
+        <p class="mon__line">${done} / ${r.planned} · ошибок ${r.failed}</p>`;
+      runBtn.disabled = true;
+    } else {
+      box.innerHTML = '<p class="empty">Обход не идёт.</p>';
+      runBtn.disabled = false;
+    }
+  }
+
+  function addLog(e) {
+    if (log.querySelector(".empty")) log.innerHTML = "";
+    const li = document.createElement("li");
+    li.className = "log__row log__row--" + e.type;
+    li.innerHTML = `<span class="log__at"></span><span class="log__type"></span><span class="log__msg"></span>`;
+    li.children[0].textContent = (e.at || "").slice(11, 19);
+    li.children[1].textContent = e.type;
+    li.children[2].textContent = e.message || e.detail || "";
+    log.prepend(li);
+    while (log.children.length > MAX_ROWS) log.lastElementChild.remove();
+  }
+
+  // EventSource reconnects on its own; we only surface the state to the user.
+  let source;
+  function connect() {
+    source = new EventSource("/monitor/stream");
+    source.addEventListener("open", () => setConn("live", "в эфире"));
+    source.addEventListener("state", (m) => renderState(JSON.parse(m.data)));
+    source.addEventListener("log", (m) => addLog(JSON.parse(m.data)));
+    source.addEventListener("error", () => setConn("down", "переподключение…"));
+  }
+  connect();
+
+  runBtn.addEventListener("click", async () => {
+    runBtn.disabled = true;                       // no double-submit while we wait
+    runMsg.textContent = "";
+    try {
+      const res = await fetch("/monitor/run", { method: "POST" });
+      const body = await res.json();
+      runMsg.textContent = body.detail;
+      runMsg.className = "mon__msg " + (res.ok ? "mon__msg--ok" : "mon__msg--warn");
+      if (!res.ok) runBtn.disabled = false;
+    } catch (err) {
+      runMsg.textContent = "не удалось отправить запрос: " + err;
+      runMsg.className = "mon__msg mon__msg--warn";
+      runBtn.disabled = false;
+    }
+  });
+})();
+</script>

diff --git a/app/youtube.py b/app/youtube.py

+"""Let's-play lookup: find the most watched playthrough, read what the blogger says.
+
+Search runs through yt-dlp's flat extractor (one request, and it already carries view
+counts). The spoken text comes from YouTube's own captions; only when there are none
+do we fall back to downloading the audio and running Whisper locally.
+
+Both of those last steps need full video extraction, which YouTube refuses from
+datacenter IPs ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot"). Point `YOUTUBE_COOKIES_FILE`
+at an exported cookie jar to lift that; without it the stage records `none` and the
+crawl carries on.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import re
+import time
+from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
+from http.cookiejar import MozillaCookieJar
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from app.config import settings
+from app.llm import chat_json
+
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS = 12_000
+TRANSCRIPT_LANGUAGES = ("en", "ru")
+
+#: Titles that are clearly not a playthrough.
+NOT_A_LETSPLAY = re.compile(
+    r"\b(trailer|teaser|announce\w*|reveal|review|обзор|трейлер|рецензи\w+|"
+    r"ost|soundtrack|music|подборка|top\s*\d+|все\s+концовки|all\s+endings)\b",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[a-zа-яё0-9]+", re.IGNORECASE)
+
+
+class YouTubeError(RuntimeError):
+    pass
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Video:
+    video_id: str
+    url: str
+    title: str
+    channel: str | None
+    view_count: int
+    duration: int
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
+        return asdict(self)
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------------- search
+
+
+def _title_words(title: str) -> set[str]:
+    """Distinctive words of a game title — short ones match everything."""
+    return {w.lower() for w in _WORD_RE.findall(title) if len(w) > 2}
+
+
+def is_letsplay(entry: dict, game_title: str) -> bool:
+    """Long enough, about this game, and not a trailer or a review."""
+    if (entry.get("duration") or 0) < settings.youtube_min_duration:
+        return False
+    title = entry.get("title") or ""
+    if NOT_A_LETSPLAY.search(title):
+        return False
+    wanted = _title_words(game_title)
+    if not wanted:
+        return False
+    haystack = _title_words(f"{title} {entry.get('description') or ''}")
+    # Most of the title has to show up; sequels and subtitles get dropped otherwise.
+    return len(wanted & haystack) / len(wanted) >= 0.6
+
+
+def _ytsearch(query: str) -> list[dict]:
+    import yt_dlp
+
+    options = {
+        "quiet": True,
+        "no_warnings": True,
+        "skip_download": True,
+        "extract_flat": True,
+        "noprogress": True,
+        "socket_timeout": 20,
+    }
+    if settings.youtube_cookies_file:
+        options["cookiefile"] = settings.youtube_cookies_file
+    with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(options) as ydl:
+        result = ydl.extract_info(query, download=False) or {}
+    return [e for e in (result.get("entries") or []) if isinstance(e, dict)]
+
+
+def search_letsplay(game_title: str) -> Video | None:
+    """Most watched playthrough of the game, or None if the search finds nothing."""
+    query = f"ytsearch{settings.youtube_search_count}:{game_title} let's play"
+    try:
+        entries = _ytsearch(query)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise YouTubeError(f"search failed: {exc}") from exc
+
+    candidates = [e for e in entries if is_letsplay(e, game_title)]
+    if not candidates:
+        return None
+    best = max(candidates, key=lambda e: e.get("view_count") or 0)
+    return Video(
+        video_id=best["id"],
+        url=best.get("url") or f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={best['id']}",
+        title=best.get("title") or "",
+        channel=best.get("channel") or best.get("uploader"),
+        view_count=best.get("view_count") or 0,
+        duration=best.get("duration") or 0,
+    )
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------- transcript
+
+
+def _cookie_session():
+    """A requests session carrying the operator's YouTube cookies, if configured."""
+    import requests
+
+    session = requests.Session()
+    path = settings.youtube_cookies_file
+    if path and Path(path).is_file():
+        jar = MozillaCookieJar(path)
+        jar.load(ignore_discard=True, ignore_expires=True)
+        session.cookies = jar
+    return session
+
+
+def fetch_subtitles(video_id: str) -> str:
+    """Caption text, auto-generated included. Empty string when there are none."""
+    from youtube_transcript_api import YouTubeTranscriptApi
+
+    api = YouTubeTranscriptApi(http_client=_cookie_session())
+    fetched = api.fetch(video_id, languages=list(TRANSCRIPT_LANGUAGES))
+    return " ".join(snippet.text.strip() for snippet in fetched if snippet.text.strip())
+
+
+def whisper_is_affordable() -> tuple[bool, str]:
+    """Whether transcribing locally is worth attempting right now."""
+    if not settings.youtube_whisper_enabled:
+        return False, "whisper disabled"
+    try:
+        import faster_whisper  # noqa: F401
+    except ImportError:
+        return False, "faster-whisper is not installed"
+    try:
+        fields = dict(line.split(":", 1) for line in Path("/proc/meminfo").read_text().splitlines())
+        free_mb = int(fields["MemAvailable"].split()[0]) // 1024
+    except Exception:
+        return False, "cannot read available memory"
+    if free_mb < settings.youtube_whisper_min_free_mb:
+        return False, f"only {free_mb} MB free, need {settings.youtube_whisper_min_free_mb}"
+    return True, f"{free_mb} MB free"
+
+
+def transcribe_audio(video_id: str, seconds_left: float) -> str:
+    """Download the opening minutes of audio and run Whisper over it."""
+    import tempfile
+
+    import yt_dlp
+    from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
+
+    span = min(settings.youtube_audio_seconds, max(int(seconds_left), 0))
+    if span < 60:
+        raise YouTubeError("not enough time left for transcription")
+
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as workdir:
+        target = Path(workdir) / "audio.%(ext)s"
+        options = {
+            "quiet": True,
+            "no_warnings": True,
+            "noprogress": True,
+            "format": "bestaudio/best",
+            "outtmpl": str(target),
+            "socket_timeout": 30,
+            # Only the opening stretch: enough to hear the verdict, cheap to fetch.
+            "download_ranges": yt_dlp.utils.download_range_func(None, [(0, span)]),
+            "force_keyframes_at_cuts": False,
+        }
+        if settings.youtube_cookies_file:
+            options["cookiefile"] = settings.youtube_cookies_file
+        with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(options) as ydl:
+            ydl.download([f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={video_id}"])
+        files = [p for p in Path(workdir).iterdir() if p.is_file() and p.stat().st_size]
+        if not files:
+            raise YouTubeError("no audio downloaded")
+
+        model = WhisperModel(settings.youtube_whisper_model, device="cpu", compute_type="int8")
+        segments, _info = model.transcribe(str(files[0]), vad_filter=True)
+        return " ".join(segment.text.strip() for segment in segments).strip()
+
+
+def get_transcript(video_id: str, seconds_left: float) -> tuple[str, str, str | None]:
+    """Returns (text, source, error). `source` is subtitles | whisper | none."""
+    try:
+        text = fetch_subtitles(video_id)
+        if text:
+            return text, "subtitles", None
+        subtitle_error = "no captions for this video"
+    except Exception as exc:
+        subtitle_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc).splitlines()[0][:200]}"
+        log.info("no subtitles for %s (%s)", video_id, subtitle_error)
+
+    affordable, why = whisper_is_affordable()
+    if not affordable:
+        return "", "none", f"{subtitle_error}; whisper skipped ({why})"
+    try:
+        text = transcribe_audio(video_id, seconds_left)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        return "", "none", f"{subtitle_error}; whisper failed: {str(exc).splitlines()[0][:200]}"
+    if not text:
+        return "", "none", f"{subtitle_error}; whisper produced nothing"
+    return text, "whisper", None
+
+
+def trim(text: str, limit: int = MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS) -> str:
+    """Keep the opening and a chunk from the middle — that is where the verdict lives."""
+    text = " ".join(text.split())
+    if len(text) <= limit:
+        return text
+    head = limit * 2 // 3
+    tail = limit - head
+    middle = (len(text) - tail) // 2
+    return f"{text[:head]}\n[…]\n{text[middle : middle + tail]}"
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- the verdict
+
+
+VERDICT_SCHEMA = '{"verdict": "строка", "highlights": ["строка"]}'
+
+
+def summarize_letsplay(game_title: str, video: Video, text: str, game_id: int | None) -> dict:
+    prompt = (
+        f"Игра: {game_title}\n"
+        f"Летсплей: «{video.title}» — канал {video.channel or 'неизвестен'}, "
+        f"{video.view_count} просмотров.\n\n"
+        "Ниже расшифровка речи блогера из этого ролика.\n\n"
+        f"{trim(text)}\n\n"
+        "Сделай заключение на русском языке. В verdict — 2-4 предложения: общее "
+        "впечатление блогера от игры, что он хвалит и что ругает. В highlights — 3-5 "
+        "коротких пунктов с конкретными моментами из ролика. Опирайся только на "
+        "расшифровку; если блогер о чём-то не говорит, не выдумывай."
+    )
+    data = chat_json(prompt, VERDICT_SCHEMA, purpose="letsplay", game_id=game_id)
+    return {
+        "verdict": str(data.get("verdict") or ""),
+        "highlights": [str(x) for x in data.get("highlights") or []],
+        "model": data.get("_model"),
+    }
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------------ the stage
+
+
+def build_letsplay(game_title: str, game_id: int | None, budget: float | None = None) -> dict:
+    """Everything for one game, as a dict of `LetsPlay` column values.
+
+    Never raises: a missing let's play is a missing feature, not a failed crawl.
+    """
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + (budget or settings.youtube_timeout)
+    record: dict = {
+        "video_id": None,
+        "url": None,
+        "title": None,
+        "channel": None,
+        "view_count": None,
+        "transcript_source": "none",
+        "transcript_chars": 0,
+        "verdict": {},
+        "model": None,
+        "error": None,
+    }
+    try:
+        video = search_letsplay(game_title)
+    except YouTubeError as exc:
+        record["error"] = str(exc)[:500]
+        return record
+    if video is None:
+        record["error"] = "подходящий летсплей не найден"
+        return record
+
+    record |= {
+        "video_id": video.video_id,
+        "url": video.url,
+        "title": video.title,
+        "channel": video.channel,
+        "view_count": video.view_count,
+    }
+
+    text, source, error = get_transcript(video.video_id, deadline - time.monotonic())
+    record["transcript_source"] = source
+    record["transcript_chars"] = len(text)
+    if not text:
+        record["error"] = (error or "нет расшифровки")[:500]
+        return record
+
+    if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+        record["error"] = "не уложились в отведённое время до вызова модели"
+        return record
+    try:
+        result = summarize_letsplay(game_title, video, text, game_id)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        record["error"] = f"LLM: {str(exc)[:400]}"
+        return record
+
+    record["model"] = result.pop("model")
+    record["verdict"] = result
+    return record

+# Replace ${DOMAIN} with the real host name, then:
+#   sudo cp deploy/nginx.conf /etc/nginx/sites-available/metacritic-ai-watch
+#   sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/metacritic-ai-watch /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
+#   sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
+#   sudo certbot --nginx -d ${DOMAIN}     # adds the TLS block below
+
+server {
+    listen 80;
+    listen [::]:80;
+    server_name ${DOMAIN};
+
+    # certbot rewrites this to a 301 once the certificate exists.
+    location / {
+        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8010;
+        proxy_http_version 1.1;
+        proxy_set_header Host              $host;
+        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP         $remote_addr;
+        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For   $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
+        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
+        proxy_read_timeout 60s;
+    }
+
+    # Server-sent events: nothing may sit in a buffer, and the connection lives
+    # longer than a normal request (the app closes it itself after 5 minutes).
+    location = /monitor/stream {
+        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8010;
+        proxy_http_version 1.1;
+        proxy_set_header Host              $host;
+        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP         $remote_addr;
+        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For   $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
+        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
+        proxy_set_header Connection        "";
+
+        proxy_buffering off;
+        proxy_cache off;
+        gzip off;
+        chunked_transfer_encoding on;
+        proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
+        proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
+    }
+
+    # Covers and the stylesheet are immutable enough to cache at the edge.
+    location ~ ^/(static|covers)/ {
+        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8010;
+        proxy_set_header Host $host;
+        expires 1d;
+        add_header Cache-Control "public";
+    }
+
+    client_max_body_size 1m;
+    access_log /var/log/nginx/metacritic-ai-watch.access.log;
+    error_log  /var/log/nginx/metacritic-ai-watch.error.log;
+}

+# Выбор LLM-модели (OpenRouter)
+
+Дата: 2026-09-06. Сравнение на одном промпте: 20 реальных пользовательских отзывов на
+Hollow Knight: Silksong → резюме по-русски строгим JSON (`likes`, `dislikes`, `summary`).
+Критерии: качество и конкретность пунктов, соблюдение JSON, время, цена за вызов.
+
+| Модель | Время | Токены (in/out) | Цена вызова | JSON | Оценка |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash | 5.4 s | 1759/640 | $0.00024 | ok | конкретно, упоминает точки сохранения, боссов, сравнение с первой частью |
+| google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite | 1.3 s | 1727/218 | $0.00026 | ok | быстро, чуть общее |
+| google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite | 1.7 s | 1727/192 | $0.00072 | ok | хорошо, в 3 раза дороже |
+| z-ai/glm-5.3-flash | 11.5 s | 1719/873 | $0.00069 | ok | очень подробно, медленно |
+| openai/gpt-4.1-mini | 2.8 s | 1714/199 | $0.00100 | ok | хорошо, в 4 раза дороже |
+| openai/gpt-5-mini | 9.4 s | 1713/723 | $0.00187 | ok | хорошо, дорого и медленно |
+| qwen/qwen3.7-flash | — | — | — | пустой ответ | отклонён |
+
+**Решение:** основная модель `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, резервная при ошибке/таймауте
+`google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite`. При 20 играх в час × 2 резюме (+1 заключение по летсплею)
+это ≈ 1500 вызовов в сутки ≈ $0.40/день на основной модели.
+
+Эмбеддингов у OpenRouter нет, поэтому «похожие игры» считаются локально (TF-IDF по
+описанию, жанрам, разработчику и платформам), без обращений к LLM.

+"""Fixture loading. Nothing in the test suite touches the network."""
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures"
+
+
+def load_html(name: str) -> str:
+    return (FIXTURES / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+
+
+def load_json(name: str) -> dict:
+    return json.loads((FIXTURES / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
+def front_door_html() -> str:
+    return load_html("games_front_door.html")

No publisher on Earth would ever fund the production of a colossal two-dimensional Metroidvania over the span of seven years, and no independent developer could realistically afford to turn such an immense ambition into reality. And yet, Hollow Knight: Silksong does exist, and it exists solely because a group of creators - deeply in love with their own work but above all blessed with extraordinary talent and the resources to make it shine - chose to invest seven years of their lives in the project. There has never been a Metroidvania so vast in content and so profound in its systems, nor one that marries such sheer scale with such painstaking artistry. On one hand, it is an experience of staggering proportions; on the other, it is enriched with the kind of craft and care one usually finds only in artisanal workshops. In the industry, it’s often said that this genre carries a fragment of the medium’s very soul. Playing through Hornet’s adventure is a reminder, plain and simple, of how beautiful it is to experience a video game made with love.</div><!----></div></div><!--[--><div class="review-footer 100 out of 100"><span>100</span></div></div> Multiplayer.it<!--]--></a><!--]--><div class="flex flex-col flex-1 w-full items-start flex-1 w-full" data-testid="review-card-quote-block"><div class="line-clamp-5 md:line-clamp-3 break-words text-base leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">Hollow Knight: Silksong is, quite simply, a video game that shouldn’t exist. No publisher on Earth would ever fund the production of a colossal two-dimensional Metroidvania over the span of seven years, and no independent developer could realistically afford to turn such an immense ambition into reality. And yet, Hollow Knight: Silksong does exist, and it exists solely because a group of creators - deeply in love with their own work but above all blessed with extraordinary talent and the resources to make it shine - chose to invest seven years of their lives in the project. There has never been a Metroidvania so vast in content and so profound in its systems, nor one that marries such sheer scale with such painstaking artistry. On one hand, it is an experience of staggering proportions; on the other, it is enriched with the kind of craft and care one usually finds only in artisanal workshops. In the industry, it’s often said that this genre carries a fragment of the medium’s very soul. Playing through Hornet’s adventure is a reminder, plain and simple, of how beautiful it is to experience a video game made with love.</div><!----></div></div><!--[--><div class="review-footer Its color and aroma are beautiful and alluring, but it&#39;s a hard liquor you can&#39;t recommend to just anyone. It would have been impeccable if, on that fine line of taste and temperament, the game had distinguished its audience solely through lucid design rather than frustrating design. md:line-clamp-3 break-words text-base leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">If the game would stand alone for itself and not as a sequel, I would probably have rated it 8/10. But since we all anticipated this game to be the great successor to the best Metroidvania there is, in Hollow Knight, I have to drop the score a little bit cause it did not fully live up to it&#39;s hype.
+
+The gameplay itself feels great, just as it already did in Hollow Knight. And the World Design with all the little secret areas to discover is again top notch, just like you would expect from Team Cherry.
+
+But in terms of Boss Fights the game is not on the same level as the first game. While there are a handful of great and fun fights, there are a lot of forgetable bosses that are either too weak or just annoying because they spawn a lot of trash mobs.
+And this is the most crucial point that I do not like about Silksong. It feels as if Team Cherry often uses the mechanic of spawning more trash mobs in boss fights as a way of increasing difficulty. This is always a lazy way to increase the difficulty of a boss and I dislike this in almost every game that does this, instead of making the boss more difficult by creating an interesting and challenging moveset.
+
+A couple bosses even have whole Trash Mob Arena fights at the start and you have to repeat them for every single try on the boss. This is such a lazy way to stretch the game and make the fights more tedious.
+
+While the game improves on some gameplay mechanics from the first, I enjoyed the charm equipment system from Hollow Knight alot more than the Crests+Gadgets from Silksong.
+
+All in all it is a good game but it is definitely a step behind the first one.</div><!----></div></div><!--[--><div class="review-footer review-footer--user game-review-footer" md:line-clamp-3 break-words text-base leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">Hollow Knight Silksong feels like a degrade from the last game team Cherry made where it was fun to navigate and enjoy the calming ambient music. However now with silksong it feels more STRESSFUL than most of the Souls genre games with many UNBALANCED aspects as I will list below.
+
+1. Most enemies even the little ones do two mask damage which is insane.
+2. Even the weakest enemies take too many hits to defeat, that puts the player in very tight spot dealing with more than one enemy at the same time.
+3. The uncalled for &quot;Runbacks&quot; when you face a boss and you lose you have to go across the map just to reach the boss with unperfect condition mostly (losing health along the way from facing enemies) and that kills the joy of playing the game by forcing the players to spend unnecessary time just to get back to fight a Boss.
+4. A lot of the tools are just nerfed clones from the first game&#39;s charms and they don&#39;t what their description say like for instance &quot;Warding Bell&quot; it shield from incoming attacks yet it fails to mention you get your healing interrupted and  lose all your silk in the process so players are left wide open with one or two masks which is the same case since you take two mask damage so are forced to lose, another instance the &quot;Magma Bell&quot; it shields from fire damage and once it does it needs to be charged or you take two masks damage if you get damaged by fire whilst it&#39;s charging, and those are just two examples.
+5. The specified sockets for the tools makes the players unable to create their own build unlike the first game.
+6. c-siteReviewScore_circle c-siteReviewScore_responsiveMobile bg-[#ffbd3f] text-[#262626] size-16 text-[2rem] leading-6 rounded-[0.375rem] rounded-full max-md:size-10 max-md:text-base max-md:leading-6 kera00<!--]--></a><!--]--><div class="flex flex-col flex-1 w-full items-start flex-1 w-full" data-testid="review-card-quote-block"><div class="line-clamp-5 md:line-clamp-3 break-words text-base leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">Don&#39;t misunderstand me. 
+
+It&#39;s by no means a bad game.
+
+starting off with the best: The platforming and general movement in this game is supreme. In some areas it feels just as snappy and satisfying as Celeste which is in fact the highest praise I can give any platformer.
+
+The art and animation is even more gorgeous than in hollow knight and especially the area design is unique and memorable. it works great with the beautiful score. 10/10 music and art.
+
+However: 
+
+Compared to Hollow Knight the characters in Silksong feel less developed or interesting. I couldn&#39;t care less about 90% of them. You have the exceptions like Sherma or Shakra but most bugs in shops, in towns or quests could be swapped out for some other one and I probably wouldn&#39;t notice. Their dialogue feels generic, the characters indistinct and unintriguing. 5/10
+
+In some areas, namely Bilewater and Sinner&#39;s Road the area mechanics, enemies and/or bench-positions just create environments so unfun and straight up frustrating to navigate and explore that it doesn&#39;t feel worth it. You&#39;re just happy to be out of there. most of the areas are good though. 7/10
+
+the bosses: This is a frustrating one. This game will give you one of the best bossfights ever created (Cogwork Dancers) then turn around and slap you in the face with Trobbio (pure RNG, little skill expression, long downtime just waiting for the guy to materialize **** gives you bosses like Lace, Widow or the Last Judge (all great) and in the same act includes the least fun bosses anyone could have ever imagined - Beastfly, Skull Tyrant or the Mossmothers. 
+
+Turns out: Just making everything hit for double damage is not the type of difficulty that makes a game fun. Making every boss also spawn in additional enemies isn&#39;t fun either. 
+Again, HK was just better in this respect. most bosses were self sufficient and found difficulty in their attack patterns, not only 2x damage. 
+Imagine if Hornet in Kingdoms Edge had just been the same as Hornet in Greenpath but she dealt 2x damage and she spawns Primal Aspids. 
+
+This is how the difficulty feels in some Silksong bosses. Every boss in Silksong is a real time commitment (for me between ~1/2 to more than 2 hours) and I just can&#39;t quite justify spending that time when I either don&#39;t feel like skill is even a relevant factor or the &quot;difficulty&quot; is just a lot of HP, double damage and external enemies. 
+
+Call it a skill issue but I just won&#39;t be bothered. 5/10
+
+TL;DR: This games exploration, movement and visual design create a beautiful world you want to go explore (for the most part anyways). Some areas&#39; mechanics and enemies are better at retaining this fun of exploration than others. The bosses are sadly somewhat of a mixed bag in terms of quality. While all pose a very significant challenge to the player some just aren&#39;t fun or rewarding, feeling like more of a test of endurance than of skill. The plot and narrative is almost insultingly explicit. Many characters feel boring and interchangeable. c-siteReviewScore_medium c-siteReviewScore_circle c-siteReviewScore_responsiveMobile bg-[#ff6b73] text-[#262626] size-16 text-[2rem] leading-6 rounded-[0.375rem] rounded-full max-md:size-10 max-md:text-base max-md:leading-6 max-md:rounded-[0.25rem] max-md:rounded-full flex flex-col items-center justify-center font-bold" title="User score 4 out of 10" aria-label="User score 4 out of 10"><span>4</span></div></div> martian0_0muse<!--]--></a><!--]--><div class="flex flex-col flex-1 w-full items-start flex-1 w-full" data-testid="review-card-quote-block"><div class="line-clamp-5 md:line-clamp-3 break-words text-base leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">Silksong is hard, but not in a rewarding way. The game relies heavily on what feels like cheap, artificial difficulty design: inflated damage, cluttered encounters, and boss mechanics that prioritize ambiguity over clarity.
+
+Fights like the second Lace encounter highlight the core issue. When attacks share similar tells but require different responses, success stops being about learning and starts feeling like guessing. That breaks the sense of fairness and makes improvement inconsistent.
+
+The pacing makes things worse. Difficulty spikes are stacked back to back with little breathing room. The game introduces optional upgrades without clearly signaling whether you should pursue them. This creates confusion about progression and leaves players feeling underpowered or misdirected.
+
+The economy adds another layer of frustration. The introduction of multiple currencies, especially tools requiring a separate and limited resource, feels poorly balanced. Early on, resources are scarce when you need them most, making retries and experimentation punishing. Later, they become abundant when they matter less. This adds friction without adding meaningful challenge.
+
+Even retrying boss fights becomes tedious. Deaths often require long backtracking through respawned enemies just to get another attempt. Failure becomes a chore instead of a learning opportunity. Rather than encouraging mastery, the game stacks frustration on top of already punishing encounters.
+
+Silksong does not build on what made Hollow Knight great: clear telegraphs, learnable fights, and satisfying challenge. Instead, it increases difficulty without adding depth. The result is a harder game that is far more frustrating than its predecessor.
+
+Challenging games can be fun. This one too often forgets that.</div><!----></div></div><!--[--><div class="review-footer review-footer--user game-review-footer" data-testid="review-card-footer" data-v-1496b33a data-v-21246f95 leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">What would otherwise be a 9/10 game is reduced to 4 over one specific, awful design choice. It&#39;s entirely expected that boss fights are about learning and multiple attempts. A good game would allow some space in between each attempt, but really only enough time to catch a breath. Silksong decided to have minute long runbacks that offer little more than a repetitive slog between each attempt. It&#39;s not nearly as much of a skill issue as it is a time issue. 
+
+As an adult with limited time for gaming, I want to spend that time enjoying myself. I&#39;ve played and beaten a lot of the games people would consider difficult, so &#39;git gud&#39; doesn&#39;t apply here. Would you choose to go to the longest line to buy groceries? Would you choose to sit in traffic? Would you read a book that had pauses in between page turns? Of course not.

leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">Silksong is another incredible journey into a kingdom not unlike Hallownest, but this time through the eyes of Hornet. Compared to her nearly hollow counterpart, The Knight, Hornet is much more of a fleshed out &quot;character,&quot; as she speaks and has a lot of personality and motivation of her own. Both approaches work well in their respective games, as The Knight&#39;s demeanor seems beffitting of a nearly dead kingdom, whereas Pharloom is a lot more lively and filled with a bunch of personalities. Another notable difference is the gender of our protagonists: Hornet is a woman. And this game is in many ways, very much about women. Most of the main cast is consisted of women, and we examine a few mother-daughter relationships, and we see through Hornet&#39;s eyes that the world is not a very friendly place to women! She is, of course, a much tougher bug than most, but there are multiple instances where gross man bugs who seriously underestimate her abilities try to harass her, and it does NOT go well for **** world Hornet is transported to is gorgeous, almost beyond belief. The drawings are so detailed and lush; exploring Pharloom is seriously magical at times. I think my favorite area was Shellwood, where bugs have evolved alongside plants, and each took on some characteristics of the **** of the biggest questions that a lot of us had going in to this game was how the gameplay and difficulty was going to compare to the first game. Hornet&#39;s arsenal of abilities and tools was a significant upgrade from The Knight&#39;s. Her incredibly agile movement feels so good to control, and all of the tools and crests she acquires give a great variety of play styles. The difficulty is the big topic that nobody seems to be able to come to a consensus on. My personal experience was that Act 1 was incredibly difficult, but Acts 2 and 3 were much easier, and at times a little too easy. I think the ease of the latter thirds of the game was largely in part to the Wanderer&#39;s crest, which I didn&#39;t start using until fairly late. I didn&#39;t mind the high difficulty of the early game because I personally just really enjoy bashing my head against a boss over and over again until I can learn their moveset to a really precise degree. And I felt that that was missing from some of the late game bosses. I had a lot of fun fighting Karmelita, who is probably my favorite boss of the game, but I beat her on my fifth try when I was expecting to be stuck on her for hours on end. For my first three attempts against her I was using the Reaper Crest, but realized that it was going to be way too hard, so I switched to Wanderer and killed her two attempts later. So I think the bosses are really excellent and the difficulty is mostly good, but the Wanderer Crest just needs some slight reworking. I don&#39;t want to be forced to nerf myself to have a higher enjoyment of the game, because I just feel stupid if I&#39;m stuck on a boss for a long time and the tools to defeat her are right at my fingertips. Nonetheless, the combat always felt incredibly fun and was a big step up from the first game in almost every way. Excellent game.</div><!----></div></div><!--[--><div class="review-footer review-footer--user game-review-footer" data-testid="review-card-footer" data-v-1496b33a data-v-21246f95 max-md:text-base max-md:leading-6 max-md:rounded-[0.25rem] max-md:rounded-full flex flex-col items-center justify-center font-bold" title="User score 10 out of 10" aria-label="User score 10 out of 10"><span>10</span></div></div> Mclintoc<!--]--></a><!--]--><div class="flex flex-col flex-1 w-full items-start flex-1 w-full" data-testid="review-card-quote-block"><div class="line-clamp-5 md:line-clamp-3 break-words text-base leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">I finished my first play-through (including Act 3). The first Hollow Knight is my favorite game of all time. Thus, I had big expectations for Silksong. I can say it is everything I hoped it would be, having all the elements of the first game in a more expansive and varied world: Precise gameplay and design, beautiful art and music, a fascinating and immersive story. It is certainly harder than Hollow Knight, but this is what I wanted and the game is never unfair. (More on this at the end)
+
+Given the long development process, there were more bugs than I expected, but I imagine these will get worked out over time. My only real complaint is the crest system. I did not like it at first. I have since warmed to it a little as it makes the game more customizable and gameplay more strategic, but overall I have just found it to be annoying. An important part of a Metroidvania is to move from powerless to powerful. The crest system is a lateral rather than upward movement and a few crests have terrible downward pogos--an essential skill for the game.
+Nevertheless, like I said, this game is everything I hoped it would be and I will be playing it for many, many more hours to come.
+
+Many have complained about the difficulty. I completed the original Hollow Knight with 112% in Steel Soul mode and completed Pantheon of Hallownest. Thus, I was well prepared for the difficulty and am so glad Team Cherry made the game harder. There is real consequence to decisions and you can see yourself getting better and better with each boss fight. I love the sense of accomplishment the game gives, and Team Cherry should be praised for this. Yes, it&#39;s not for everyone, but, as I said, the game is never unfair, and it gives someone who loved Hollow Knight just what they wanted. Git Gud!</div><!----></div></div><!--[--><div class="review-footer review-footer--user game-review-footer" data-testid="review-card-footer" data-v-1496b33a data-v-21246f95 md:line-clamp-3 break-words text-base leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">Silksong is the first Hollow Knight game I have played and it will be the only. 
+
+I have played video games for all of my life and often play on hard modes, but Hollow Knight has no difficulty settings yet is unbelievable impossible to play. I spend more hours watching how-to videos on youtube than actually playing the game, and each arena/miniboss/boss takes around 4 hours or 50-100 attempts each. 
+
+But the difficulty isn’t even the worst thing. Every battle is far from a save point meaning you have to monotonously trek/fight past multiple enemies and jumps on the way back to the arena, and if you die before reaching your previous death location you lose all the currency you have worked hours for. So each time you die, you lose any hope of gaining better weapons or exploring alternative areas due to having no currency to achieve these plans. 
+
+The game style and art is beautiful, but the difficulty and mechanics make it the only game I’ve ever felt physically angry while playing. You are better off having never started.</div><!----></div></div><!--[--><div class="review-footer review-footer--user game-review-footer" data-testid="review-card-footer" data-v-1496b33a leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">My vote for GOTY will definitely for Silksong. First time ever, I bought a digital game at full price. The fact that they make it affordable just made me want to fully support them.
+
+Besides that, the game runs flawlessly on Switch. No lag or performance issue, visual is the same like the original Hollow Knight which great, vibrant and lively.
+
+Now to the gameplay itself. Yes, it does 2/3x times harder than the original Hollow Knight but I would argue that we&#39;re just not fully utilizing the new moveset and get used to Hornet agility. The fact that we can heal 3 health bar right away is already a sign that the dev want us to get more into action instead finding time to heal. On the other side there are more tools so I see no reason for it being too difficult or punishing. For context, I finish the game and reach true ending, not completing it yet.
+
+Besides that, we also get 7 different play style which nuts. Some are lackluster but the fact they provide us with 7 different approach in combat is amazing. Plus, we can synergies each tool to specific play style so we can play around to find combo that suit our style. 
+
+I&#39;m 60+ hours in and there&#39;s still so much more to discover. With that amount of content, I feel the value of the game is way much more than what its priced. Well recommended and must buy for metroidvania fans. Don&#39;t let difficulty holds you back but one thing I can warn you = If you didn&#39;t manage to finish Hollow Knight due to its difficulty and you hate it, skip this game, you&#39;ll hate it even more.</div><!----></div></div><!--[--><div class="review-footer review-footer--user game-review-footer" data-testid="review-card-footer" data-v-1496b33a data-v-21246f95 data-v-1a76345f><!--[--><span md:line-clamp-3 break-words text-base leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">I&#39;ve been on a rollercoaster with Silksong. From highly dissapointed, to love, and then dissapointment again. I have now settled on this; I love it mechanically but it doesn&#39;t quite do it for me on many other levels. In this way it feels like my relationship with Dark Souls 3 in comparison to Dark Souls 1, mechanically much improved, stuffed with cool toys and details, but a lesser game in some ways, lacking a the vibe and soul that made me lovr the earlier game.
+
+I wrote my first review of Silksong in a bit of a temper. I thought this is too hard, they went bananas with the difficulty. I struggled with many bosses. I put the game down for a while at the end of act 1. Picked it back up a few days later and replayed from the start. I found a few more tools, got more practice, and enjoyed it more, eventually cracked into act 2. I was killing bosses in less attempts, getting through the game way faster. I&#39;ve started about 4 or 5 games now and I am contemplating the speedrunning challenge. All my earlier complaints about difficulty, pacing, or the economy have melted as I have  practiced and (thankfully) improved, and my knowlege of the game has grown.
+
+It&#39;s certainly a challenge though and if you aren&#39;t great at action video gaming like me it might take you a lot of practice, time, and patience to get competent at, and through Silksong. 
+
+I am left feeling a little dissapointed that there isn&#39;t quite the same magic as I felt there was in HK, and there isn&#39;t anything really that innovative. Most of Silksongs tricks have been done before, most of the surprises feel like stuff we&#39;ve seen before in Dark Souls or Bloodborne. Which are fun references but I am disappointed that the game lacks any really interesting twists of its own.
+
+In short, it&#39;s good, well priced, challenging, feels great in the hands once you get competent enough to enjoy it, unfortunately not quite as stellar as it&#39;s predecessor or I want it to be. I doubt DLC can push it up there but hey, we will have to see.</div><!----></div></div><!--[--><div class="review-footer review-footer--user game-review-footer" data-testid="review-card-footer" Torby<!--]--></a><!--]--><div class="flex flex-col flex-1 w-full items-start flex-1 w-full" data-testid="review-card-quote-block"><div class="line-clamp-5 md:line-clamp-3 break-words text-base leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">30 years after the release of Super Metroid and almost 15 years after the release of Dark Souls, Hollow Knight: Silksong creates a new gold standard by fusing together and mastering the best parts of both games and their genres. 2017&#39;s Hollow Knight already did this to some extent, but personally I found it to be too bleak and too unpolished in its level design. I now appreciate it more however, as it prepared me for this adventure. 
+
+Hollow Knight: Silksong sports breathtaking visuals and an immersive soundtrack that takes you away into Pharloom, an expansive world that never fails to surprise you without feeling too overwhelming. Every area has distinct environments and enemies, with intuitive level design and paths that you quickly get used to traversing. Inaccessible areas are clearly marked as such, with clues that will have you returning later to explore more. These are basics of a Metroidvania, but it is seldom done this precisely and to this scale. Even after putting 50 hours into the game, I still found new paths that interconnected areas in unexpected ways and gave me that &quot;aha!&quot; moment. Just as the creators promised, this is a handcrafted and gorgeous world to explore, from the depths of the Deep Docks to the High Halls of the Citadel.
+
+The story borrows heavily from Fromsoftware&#39;s style, with a bleak, overarching story that you can affect the outcome of, and with its memorable characters that you follow and interact with throughout the world. But as opposed to Dark Souls, it&#39;s much easier to follow and track. The new quest system is surprisingly fleshed out, and pairs perfectly with the backtracking that is normally found in the genre. Suddenly I found myself donating to charity, participating in a race, or even buying a house! And imagine my relief when I found out that you can 100% the game on your first save file, even after doing the &quot;standard&quot; ending and &quot;missing&quot; things in one of the game&#39;s acts. Whereas for instance Elden Ring forces you to replay the entire game&#39;s 30+ hour campaign to see a different ending.
+
+Hollow Knight: Silksong is tough, but fair. It gives the player all the necessary tools to succeed and more, but also trusts them with the responsibility of finding them and learning how they work. It follows in the footsteps of its predecessors and rewards experimentation and exploration to a high degree. The new crest system allows players to alter Hornet&#39;s moveset, and the new tools gives you a plethora of ways to fight. The movement and gameplay itself is extremely versatile and responsive, more so than in Hollow Knight. Fighting enemies and bosses has never been more fun!
+
+So, what are the negatives? The challenge is significant, and may seem daunting. And since the game goes for a &quot;show don&#39;t tell&quot; style, players might find themselves stuck at different points, not knowing how to beat a boss or progress a specific quest.  While I do think the game could use an accessibility option, I also respect the creator vision and their decision to keep the game as is. No game is for everyone, and that is especially true here. But *if* you want to experience Silksong, don&#39;t be discouraged it&#39;s reputation. The required boss fights for the standard ending are completely surmountable, and looking up how to get a few useful items will quickly get you ahead if you&#39;re struggling. And even if you keep dying, the game rarely feels unfair or frustrating.
+
+That is not to say there aren&#39;t critique worthy parts of the game. The in-game economy is rough at times, and some boss fights or &quot;runbacks&quot; are more difficult than they need to be. It&#39;s hard to pin these down as truly negative aspects, as they elevate other parts of the experience. The limited ammo for tools are there because they do make boss fights significantly easier. And the frustrating areas such as &quot;Bilewater&quot;, tests the player&#39;s skills and offers an optional challenge to who dares take it. That being said, yes, the game pushes the bar too far at times, undoubtedly frustrating many players.
+
+If that&#39;s the case, why is it deserving of a perfect score? To me, personally, it&#39;s the extreme amount of polish, value for its price tag, and the feeling of &quot;extra&quot; that I&#39;m left with after playing it. You could finish this as a standard Metroidvania experience in 20 hours and be left satisfied. But as opposed to most other Metroidvania experiences out there, this game just keeps on giving and giving if you put more time into it. And finally, I have to talk about the boss fights. There is an huge gauntlet of challenging bosses feel amazing to master. Their variety, scale and polish is nothing short of perfection. Even as a huge Fromsoftware fan, I have to say that I&#39;ve never had this much fun with bosses in a game before.
+
+Hollow Knight: Silksong offers an amazing amount of value for its price tag, and expands upon and develops the Metroidvania genre to new heights. Honestly, I can&#39;t praise it enough. Thanks for reading.</div><!----></div></div><!--[--><div class="review-footer review-footer--user game-review-footer" data-testid="review-card-footer" data-v-1496b33a data-v-21246f95 DanteLa<!--]--></a><!--]--><div class="flex flex-col flex-1 w-full items-start flex-1 w-full" data-testid="review-card-quote-block"><div class="line-clamp-5 md:line-clamp-3 break-words text-base leading-normal" data-testid="review-quote-text">Warum Silksong aus meiner Perspektive kein gutes Spiel ist...
+
+Hollow Knight: Silksong ist ein wunderschönes Spiel. Eine atemberaubende bezaubernde Welt mit vielen Verstecken und Geheimnissen. Viele liebevoll gestaltete Gebiete. Von Lavewelten und alten Schmieden zu Städten einer sterbenden Hochkultur. Verträumte Gärten, mythische Wälder, dunkle Abgründe und göttliche Welten. Es ist alles dabei. Eine kluge, in sich schlüssige Welt. Das ist den Entwicklern sehr gut gelungen.
+
+Hornet als Protagonistin ist auch faszinierend. Dieses Mal eine Heldin, die redet, Dialoge führt und die Welt auf eine neue Art kennenlernt. Die Geschichte, die man mehr und mehr entschlüsselt je tiefer wir in die Welt eindringen, verzaubert und berührt. Eine Geschichte mit Humor, Drama und jede Menge Wirren. Dies ist auch sehr gut gelungen. 
+
+Das Gameplay, Platforming und Kämpfen macht auch sehr viel Spass. Das Rumprobieren mit verschiedenen Werkzeugen und Fähigkeiten, die man entdeckt sind schon cool. Und es gibt jede Menge Möglichkeit kreativ zu sein und sich auszuleben. Auch die Gegner und Bosse sind sehr verschieden und überraschen immer wieder. Die Bewegungen sind flüssig. Ich habe nie irgendwelche Lacks oder Fehler festgestellt. 
+
+Auch der Preis der Entwickler ist sehr entgegenkommend und eine Liebeserklärung an die Community.
+
+Trotzt allem ist Silksong für mich kein gutes Spiel. Die Wertung wäre notmalerweise bei 9 bis 10. 
+
+Hinzukommt aber der Schwierigkeitsgrad. Ich bin Schwierigkeit gewöhnt. Von Elden Ring zu Dark Souls habe ich jedes Soulslike durch. Jede Herausforderung gemeistert. Es war hart und schwierig. Aber das Lernen und das Meistern hat immer letzten Endes Spass gemacht. 
+
+Aber Silksong hat mir die Freude genommen. Bosse fordernd zu gestalten ist immer gut. Zu lernen und sich zu verbessern ist das ultimative Gamingerlebnis. Zumindest für mich. Dieses Gefühl hatte ich hier nicht. Es gab Kämpfe, die gut waren. 
+Aber dann gab es einfach Passagen, wo erstmal eine schwierigr Platforming Abschnitt kommt und dann der Boss. Wenn der Boss einen besiegt. Muss das Platforming nochmal gemacht werden. Und das ist mega frustrierend. 
+Klar lernt man das irgendwann. Klar meistert man das Plattforming. Klar legt man irgendwann den Boss. Aber es fühlt sich dann nur noch wie eine monotone stupide Wiederholung an. Vor allem frustrierend ist es wenn man einen so mega schwierigen Abschnitt schafft und es dann nicht mal eine Belohnung gibt. Stattdessen kommt der Absturz in ein schwierigeres Gebiet. Indem man zusätzlich gefangen ist und auch noch Safepoint immer wieder kaufen muss. Das sind Designentscheidungen die mich insgesamt frustriert haben.
+
+Auch wichtige Items hinter Quests zu verstecken, die langwierig und teilweise zufallsabhängig sind, finde ich genauso unverständlich. Genauso Safepoints nach einer schwierigen Platforming Passage mit Fallen zu bestücken, finde ich auch daneben. Das ist einfach nicht witzig. 
+Irgendwann hat sich dieses Spiel dann nur noch wie eine langweillige, monotone Wiederholung ohne richtige Erfolgserlebnisse angefühlt.
+Aufgrunddessen gibt es auch ein massive Abwertung meinerseits. Auf 7 Punkte insgesamt.</div><!----></div></div><!--[--><div class="review-footer review-footer--user game-review-footer" data-testid="review-card-footer" data-v-1496b33a data-v-21246f95 There is an huge gauntlet of challenging bosses feel amazing to master. Their variety, scale and polish is nothing short of perfection.
